Threat.value: I am on high alert when I hear unexpected or loud sounds
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: I have permanently changed for the worse
My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy

issues.item: Hard to Recall Deliberately: When I try to deliberately remember what happened I find it difficult to access the memory
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Hard to Recall Deliberately' conflicts with 'Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.' Deliberate retrieval difficulty and very easy verbal access are opposing states and are hard to reconcile as describing the same patient at the same time, especially alongside 'Overwhelm on Recall,' which implies traumatic recall is effortful and dysregulating rather than easy to discuss.

issues.item: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'I can talk about what happened very easily' directly conflicts with 'When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop.' At this severity level and with strong Trigger↔Memory and Memory→Threat links, these two memory items describe opposing levels of accessibility/distress and are hard to reconcile as the same current presentation.

issues.item: Triggers: Authority Commands: Being given orders or instructions
issues.explanation: The trigger set is hard to reconcile with stalking as the index trauma: 'authority commands' and especially 'bicycle' do not show an evident clinical link to the reported trauma, and the profile provides no memory or appraisal content that would make these idiosyncratic triggers understandable.

Threat items emphasize broad interpersonal attack and generic danger vigilance (loud sounds, scanning exits, watching others for harm), which fits assault/combat/fire trauma better than stalking. For stalking, one would expect threat focused more on being followed, approached, monitored, contacted, or found by the perpetrator.

issues.item: Threat: Threat in Sounds: I am on high alert when I hear unexpected or loud sounds
issues.explanation: 'I am a weak person' sits awkwardly with this profile and occupation unless supported by appraisal content about failure to protect oneself or family; here the other appraisals center on permanent damage and fear of going crazy, so the weakness item feels less coherent with the stalking-specific formulation than those items.

vignette: Sami, a 37-year-old Middle Eastern firefighter, has been grappling with overwhelming anxiety and distress following a traumatic stalking incident. The event occurred several months ago when he was repeatedly followed by an individual who seemed to be monitoring his every move. Since then, Sami's daily life has become increasingly strained as he struggles with intense triggers that remind him of the harrowing experience. Whenever Sami rides his bicycle to work or sees any location associated with the stalking, he feels a sudden surge of panic and is immediately transported back to those frightening moments. The sound of unexpected noises or hearing someone following closely behind on foot sends shivers down his spine, triggering vivid flashbacks that overwhelm him emotionally. "I just freeze up," Sami explains, "the memory hits me so hard that I can barely breathe." This triggered recall leaves him feeling unable to articulate the intensity of what he experienced. Sami's perceptions and fears have deeply altered his sense of self. He believes he has been permanently damaged by this experience and now views himself as weak for reacting so strongly to it. His concerns about going crazy add another layer of distress, further isolating him from those around him. The more Sami reflects on the stalking incident and how it has affected him, the stronger his negative appraisals become, reinforcing a cycle of fear and helplessness. These negative beliefs not only heighten Sami's sense of vulnerability but also intensify his threat perceptions. He constantly scans for exits whenever he enters any room or building, watches others closely to ensure no one is about to harm him, and remains on high alert for unexpected sounds that could trigger another flashback. The more vigilant he becomes, the more convinced he is that he is indeed weak and going crazy. Sami's occupational environment as a firefighter adds to his stress. He often feels overwhelmed when riding his bicycle to work or patrolling familiar areas where the stalking occurred. "What frightens me most," he says, "is knowing that I can be triggered at any moment, even in places I should feel safe." The trauma has strained his relationships with colleagues and family, as he withdraws from social interactions due to the constant fear of being followed or watched. Over time, Sami's avoidance behaviors have led to significant changes in how he operates both personally and professionally. He avoids certain routes during work shifts, which has made it difficult for him to fulfill his duties effectively. His wife has noticed a marked change in his demeanor; he is more distant and often distracted by the constant fear of being stalked again. The weight of these experiences finally pushed Sami to seek help when he realized that his functioning was severely compromised. He hopes that therapy can provide him with tools to manage his fears and negative appraisals, allowing him to reclaim a sense of normalcy in his life. Despite feeling permanently damaged, Sami is determined to confront the trauma and regain control over his thoughts and behaviors. Sami's story underscores the complex interplay between triggers, memories, threat perceptions, and negative appraisals following a traumatic event. His journey highlights how these components can form a self-reinforcing cycle of distress that impacts both his personal life and professional responsibilities.
